title: Focal Epilepsy in the Gulf Cooperation Council: Practice Patterns and Pathways Beyond Drug Resistance
content: Background: Management of focal epilepsy requires appropriate medication selection, reliable recognition of drug resistance and access to comprehensive assessment. Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) publications describe practice patterns in prescribing, specialist services and surgical outcomes, but the connections between these components remain incompletely characterised. Objective: To synthesise GCC practice patterns, evaluate pathways beyond recognised drug resistance and identify priorities for adult focal epilepsy care. Methods: This structured narrative review combined PubMed retrieval on 17 November 2026 with targeted searches through 19 November 2026. Purposive selection and qualitative appraisal distinguished GCC patient and service evidence from international treatment studies, guidance and proposed implementation measures. Findings: Regional cohorts document monotherapy in general epilepsy care and frequent levetiracetam prescribing. Drug-resistant cohorts demonstrate established and newer medication use without defining comparative effectiveness or treatment sequences. Incomplete treatment histories, adherence difficulties and variable referral thresholds identify potential weaknesses in recognising resistance and completing assessment. A survey of 17 GCC monitoring units demonstrates variation in diagnostic practice; surgical series document outcomes in selected patients, including MRI-negative adults. International evidence supports further pharmacological benefit after drug resistance, but short-term seizure freedom does not establish durable remission or justify routine postponement of evaluation. Regional longitudinal evidence remains insufficient to determine whether expanding treatment choice improves access or outcomes. Conclusions: GCC pathways should link documented medication trials to comprehensive assessment, multidisciplinary decisions and shared continuing-care responsibilities. Medication optimisation should proceed alongside evaluation. Proposed indicators distinguish treatment-responsive deferral from incomplete access and assess seizure control, tolerability, patient priorities and follow-up. Prospective testing is required before endorsement.
